decomp-workbench compare:
usage: decomp-workbench compare [-h] [--symbol NAME] [--explain-keys]
                                [--color {auto,always,never}]
                                [--section SECTION] [--objdump OBJDUMP]
                                [--json] [--cross-rom] [--show-diff]
                                [--fail-on-mismatch] [--built-from PATH]
                                [--allow-stale] [--watch-rows ROWS]
                                [--by-region SRC] [--by-region-limit N]
                                [--census KEY=VALUE[,KEY=VALUE...]]
                                target candidate

Compare instruction words, relocations, structure, and registers.

positional arguments:
  target                reference object
  candidate             candidate object

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --symbol, --function NAME
                        compare only this exact symbol; --function is the same
                        option. Omitting it compares the whole section
                        positionally - only safe when both objects hold the
                        same single function.
  --explain-keys        print the metric registry (label, JSON key, meaning)
                        and exit
  --color {auto,always,never}
                        ANSI coloring; every label and annotation is present
                        without it
  --section SECTION     object section (default: .text)
  --objdump OBJDUMP     GNU-compatible MIPS objdump; auto-detected when
                        omitted
  --json                emit JSON
  --cross-rom           accept structural cross-ROM evidence; never call it an
                        object-exact source match
  --show-diff           print every differing site, grouped by class
  --fail-on-mismatch    return exit 1 unless exact, or structurally exact with
                        --cross-rom
  --built-from PATH     an input the compared artifacts were built from -- the
                        source, the object, the ELF. Repeatable. The command
                        refuses when a compared artifact is older than one of
                        these
  --allow-stale         report the staleness and continue anyway, instead of
                        refusing. The report is printed either way
  --watch-rows ROWS     watch these positional rows and print a healed/broken
                        column for each (. healed, X broken, ? out of range).
                        Takes 49,1620,1677, or r49=49,cx2=1620 to name the
                        columns, or @probes.json for a named set. Scalar
                        metrics conflate schedule with allocation and over-
                        charge block permutations; a signature over rows you
                        chose because they discriminate does neither
  --by-region SRC       group the differing words by the source construct that
                        emitted them, ranked by count, each citing SRC:line.
                        Attribution is call-relocation anchoring: rows are
                        bracketed between the two calls around them, never
                        interpolated to a line, and the report states its own
                        coverage
  --by-region-limit N   show only the top N regions (default: 12; 0 for all)
  --census KEY=VALUE[,KEY=VALUE...]
                        assert reported values; exit 3 if any predicate fails
                        (2 for an unknown key), and print one PASS/FAIL line
                        each. Repeatable

options:

  --symbol, --function NAME

                        omitted
  --candidate-listing PATH
                        the assembly listing ugen wrote for the candidate,
                        used to report whether schedule-divergent sites sit at
                        .loc statement-line boundaries; the IDO driver keeps
                        it beside the object when you pass `cc -K`, and `ugen
                        -l` writes it directly
  --trace PATH          an instrumented-uopt globalcolor trace
                        (CSAVE/CUP/CDX). A declined force or a regsleft=0
                        contest in it settles ownership as a measurement, so
                        the verdict reads ownership_basis=trace instead of
                        heuristic
  --trace-proc N        scope --trace to one procedure; a trace covers a whole
                        compilation and a residual is one function's
  --trace-web N         scope --trace to one web within the procedure
  --ladder PATH         a CDX log carrying CDX_SYMTAB=1 itable records;
                        supplies the declared-local count the stack-home lever
                        is measured against
  --force-result PATH   a decomp-workbench-oracle-sweep-v1 JSON from a
                        recorded CDX_FORCE run. It answers a question no
                        source evidence does: words=0 under a force proves the
                        target's colours are legal in this web graph, and a
                        declined or instruction-adding force proves they are
                        not
  --ring-trace PATH     a DKWB_UGEN_TRACE free-list log; supplies ring pops
                        per source line, which is what names the construct
                        that bought or sold one
  --emit-trace PATH     a DKWB-EMIT-V1 ugen emit-provenance log; supplies the
                        line-order conflicts the loop-header join removes
  --as1-trace PATH      an as1 `cc -Wa,-R` scheduler trace. The deciding key
                        of a selection settles the line question outright:
                        decided on lineno the line lever reaches it, decided
                        above lineno nothing in the source does
  --source PATH         the candidate's C. Read only to check what the line a
                        ring trace charged actually contains: each pop-cost
                        rule was measured on one construct, and without the
                        line no temp-ring edit family is named
  --lever-proc N        scope --ladder, --ring-trace and --emit-trace to one
                        procedure ordinal, for the same reason --trace-proc

  --report-regs         report per-aligned-index register operands, matching

the gate a configuration edit has to pass before either number means anything:
the candidate link must reproduce the shipped one exactly. `plan` merges the
reports into one ranked, gated remediation queue. Run `decomp-workbench shift
audit --help` and its neighbours.

usage: decomp-workbench shift audit [-h] --map FILE --image FILE [--elf FILE]
                                    [--pins FILE] [--symbol-addrs FILE]
                                    [--blob SECTION] [--blobs {auto}]
                                    [--no-blob SECTION]
                                    [--emit-whitelist FILE] [--whitelist FILE]
                                    [--limit N] [--json]
                                    [--census KEY=VALUE[,KEY=VALUE...]]
                                    [--explain-keys] [--width COLUMNS]
                                    [--pager {auto,always,never}]

Inventory a linked project's addresses without building anything. The pin half
reads the project's own linker-input symbol files and says which addresses
follow the layout (`gMainMemoryPool = main_BSS_END`) and which are written
down (`D_B0000574 = 0xB0000574`). The scan half reads the image's data and
blob regions and reports every word holding a value inside the movable VRAM
window -- with the features that discriminate a real address reference from a
packed field, a repeated struct constant, a fixed-point table value, or build-
machine garbage. Tiers rank how confidently a word is a reference, never how
dangerous it is: a linked ROM keeps no relocations, so only a shifted relink
(`shift rehearse`) can say which references actually move.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --map FILE            the linked `ld -Map` file
  --image FILE          the linked image the map describes
  --elf FILE            the linked ELF this map and image came from. Optional,
                        and it buys two things the map cannot see. A pin an
                        object in the link already defines: GNU ld lets a
                        script assignment override an object's definition with
                        no warning, and keeps the losing definition's size on
                        the surviving absolute symbol -- so the check is exact
                        rather than a heuristic, and needs no shift. Those
                        pins are `shadowing-pin`, and deleting one is byte-
                        identical at the current layout. And whether
                        --pins/--symbol-addrs itself is complete: an absolute
                        symbol the link carries that no supplied file names is
                        `pins_missing_sources` -- the -T file nobody handed
                        this run
  --pins FILE           an ld-script symbol-assignment file such as
                        ver/symbols/undefined_syms.txt; repeatable
  --symbol-addrs FILE   a splat `symbol_addrs` file; repeatable. Read with the
                        same grammar as --pins, plus the `key:value`
                        attributes splat writes in the trailing comment
  --blob SECTION        treat this output section as opaque bytes: scanned,
                        but never split by its input records and never
                        attributed to a symbol. Repeatable. Use it for DMA'd
                        segments and boot code, whose VMA is a load target
                        rather than a place code lives
  --blobs {auto}        `auto` adopts the blob set the map's own input records
                        imply -- every section all of whose objects are raw
                        binaries. The report prints that suggestion either
                        way; this is what says yes to it. --blob still adds on
                        top and --no-blob subtracts
  --no-blob SECTION     keep this output section out of the blob set whatever
                        `--blobs auto` suggested. Repeatable. Naming the same
                        section with --blob and --no-blob is refused rather
                        than resolved by precedence
  --emit-whitelist FILE
                        write a whitelist skeleton drafted from this run's own
                        evidence -- hardware-window pins and kseg0 pins below
                        the movable window floor -- each entry commented out,
                        marked `# REVIEW:`, and carrying the pin it came from.
                        Refuses to overwrite an existing file; the audit runs
